title: Commensal bacteria can hijack planarian morphogenesis to cause two-headed regeneration

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Commensal bacteria can hijack planarian morphogenesis to cause two-headed regeneration

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Like parasites that manipulate host neurobehavioural systems, commensal bacteria can override the default planarian morphogenetic control system and cause two-headed regeneration.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the planarian morphogenetic control system too can be hijacked not only by bioengineers (as described above) but also by commensal bacteria which can over-ride the default system and lead to two-headed regeneration (Williams et al. 2020).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation”. Scope: Planarian flatworms and their commensal microbiota (Williams et al. 2020)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The bacterial intervention and head-number outcome are concrete and can have strong causal controls. Public availability of animal-level records is uncertain, and the manipulative 'hijack' framing is not required by the phenotype.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare head-number outcomes in germ-reduced planaria colonized with the candidate commensal, vehicle controls, and heat-killed or mutant bacteria, then test clearance and re-colonization rescue. Increased two-headed regeneration attributable to live bacteria confirms the experimental result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Antibiotic or colonization procedures can independently alter regeneration.

Matched microbiome and morphology data may not be public.

Override and hijack imply function beyond causation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.93
data existence: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head number under a defined bacterial treatment is a direct experimental endpoint, and the 2020 paper reports it for this commensal and for indole. Those measurements are not a deposited count table or expression series that can be reprocessed. The result can be reassessed from the publication and cannot be recomputed from open raw data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regenerate Dugesia japonica fragments exposed to the endogenous Aquitalea isolate or to indole, against microbiome-depleted controls, and score permanent two-headed anatomy. Two-headed animals specifically under the bacterium or indole, and not under depletion alone, would support hijacking of the default pattern; no change in head number would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The RNA-seq mentioned with the indole treatment was not found as a public series, and head-number counts are in the paper.

Indole has several host effects, so a two-headed outcome need not mean the morphogenetic circuit was overridden in the same way as a bioelectric rewrite.

operationalizability: 0.85
